questions.q: At which type of plate boundary do plates slide past each other, causing earthquakes but no volcanoes?
questions.why: Conservative (transform) boundaries, such as the San Andreas Fault, cause earthquakes but no volcanoes.

questions.q: Which landform forms where two continental plates collide?
questions.why: Neither continental plate sinks, so the crust crumples upwards, e.g. the Himalayas.

questions.q: The point on the Earth's surface directly above where an earthquake starts is the:
questions.why: The focus is underground; the epicentre is directly above it on the surface.

questions.q: Explain how earthquake-proof building design reduces the loss of life in an earthquake.
questions.model: Buildings with steel frames, reinforced concrete and flexible foundations absorb or sway with the shaking, so they are less likely to collapse on people.
points: named design feature (steel frame, flexible foundations, reinforced concrete)
absorbs shaking so buildings do not collapse and fewer people are killed
